nodes.name: Commits In (Webhook)
nodes.notes: Entry point of the pipe. Anything that has repository observations POSTs them here: the collector workflow, the backfill replay of cached JSON files, or you with curl. Unauthenticated by design for now — the stack binds 127.0.0.1 only. Before this is exposed on a network it needs header auth, because anything that can reach this URL can write rows.

nodes.name: Validate Payload
nodes.notes: Checks the shape before any SQL runs. Four payloads arrive here: repository records, an archive list, run-claim requests and run summaries. Known states: complete, partial, error, stale, empty (no commits — GitHub 409) and pending (known, not yet collected). Only 'complete' records prune.

nodes.name: Save Batch
nodes.notes: The only writer to the product database. One statement, one transaction: upsert repositories, archive repositories absent upstream (never delete them, so their commits survive as history), prune commits only for records that carry a complete and authoritative commit list, then upsert the rest. Two gates stop a partial or skipped record from deleting rows it never fetched: source_state must be 'complete', and commits_omitted must not be set.

nodes.name: Reply
nodes.notes: Returns the counts so the caller can verify what happened instead of assuming: repositories upserted, commits pruned, commits seen, commits new. The backfill uses these numbers to check itself.

nodes.name: Run Claim
nodes.notes: The run lease: acquire or release the single-row claim that allows one collector run at a time. Atomic on purpose — INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE expired means two simultaneous runs cannot both acquire, which a read-then-write would allow. Lives here because this workflow is the only writer to the product database; the collector asks over the pipe and stays read-only.

nodes.name: Is Run Claim?
nodes.notes: Two payload shapes arrive here: repository records and run-claim requests. Keeping them in one webhook means one pipe and one writer; the branch keeps each branch doing exactly one thing.

nodes.name: Save Run
nodes.notes: Records what a run did, and what happened to each repository inside it: one row in mnemora_runs, one row per repository in mnemora_telemetry. One statement, so a run can never appear in the run book without its detail. Telemetry exists because successful executions are not retained by n8n here — without it, a slow or capped repository leaves no trace once the run ends.

nodes.name: Is Run Summary?
nodes.notes: Third payload shape on the same endpoint: repository records, run claims, and now run summaries. Each branch does exactly one write.
